title: Design an Authoritative Online Chess Platform
prompt:
Design a global online chess service. Players request opponents by rating, region, and time control; the matching range may widen while they wait. Explain the request-intake and asynchronous matchmaking flow, including queue organization, cancellation, duplicate delivery, and a matcher that crashes while forming a game.

Support rated and timed games, reconnection, move history, and spectators. A game needs one consistent ordering of accepted moves, and clients cannot be trusted to report elapsed clock time. Define move and clock contracts, persistence, live updates, retries, owner failure, and recovery. State scale and latency assumptions.

response.placeholder: Start with request intake, matchmaking queues, and atomic match creation. Then define the game authority, clock contract, durable write boundary, and reconnect path.
response.reference_answer:
## Request intake and matchmaking
A request handler validates the player and records a durable matchmaking request with an idempotency key. An asynchronous matching service selects compatible requests by time control, region, and a rating window that widens with wait time. Explain how workers find eligible buckets without allowing older requests to starve.

Claim both requests and commit a match atomically, with at most one active match per request. A cancellation racing with matching must have one observable winner. Duplicate queue deliveries find the same request state; an expired worker claim can be retried without pairing either player twice. Publish game-creation work after the durable match commit, and make game creation idempotent so a crash between these steps is recoverable.

## Authority and API
Creating or joining a game returns a game ID and player role. A move carries a client idempotency key and expected game version; the server validates turn, legality, and version.

## Per-game serialization
Route every command for one game to a fenced owner shard. The owner derives clocks from server timestamps, appends the validated move and resulting clock state durably, updates a latest snapshot, and only then publishes the new version. There is no global ordering requirement. A lease epoch prevents a former owner from publishing after failover.

## Reconnect and failure
A reconnecting client receives a snapshot plus events after its cursor. Clocks continue while disconnected. Persist timeout decisions as delayed durable work, not only an in-memory timer. Replicas and an event log allow a new fenced owner to recover.

## Operations
Rate-limit commands and spectators separately, bound hot-game fan-out, paginate history, and measure matchmaking wait and widening, duplicate-match prevention, move validation latency, owner failover, reconnect gaps, illegal moves, and clock disputes.

## Progressive Hints
1. One game needs serial order; the whole service does not.
2. Persist before broadcasting.
3. A client clock is display data, not authority.
